scores.claim_text: Planet Labs Federal, Inc. is a NISPOM-cleared U.S. subsidiary performing classified work for the U.S. government.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts + federal_presence on Planet Labs Federal
scores.M_value: PLANET LABS FEDERAL, INC. (UEI TFCJCMKNHT74) confirmed in SAM; 22 federal awards FY23-FY25 totaling $58.07M; agencies include DoD (10 awards), NASA (4), USDA/Interior/Commerce. Aggregating all name variants (including PBC + Inc.): 89 contracts and $165.5M across DoD, NASA, Interior, USDA, DOC, HHS, DOJ, DHS.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Planet Labs Federal exists as a registered federal contractor with extensive multi-agency footprint. Federal subsidiary claim is corroborated cleanly.

scores.claim_text: Defense & Intelligence revenue grew to $180.232M in FY2026 (vs $116.281M FY2025, $94.555M FY2024).
scores.M_check: usaspending federal presence across PL name variants — aggregate $$ obligated vs disclosed D&I revenue trajectory
scores.M_value: Federal contracts (89 awards, FY23-FY26 window) total $165.5M obligated. Mix: NASA, DoD-Navy (NIWC), Interior, USDA, DOC. Sample DoD descriptions: 'PLANETSCOPE DATA' ($7.5M, N6600125P6327); 'ELECTRO OPTICAL SATELLITE DATA IMAGERY SUBSCRIPTIONS' ($6.7M, N6600125P6016); 'SAT-EO SUBSCRIPTION' for SE Asia ($6.5M, N6600124P6048). NASA top awards: ELECTRO OPTICAL DATA REQUIREMENT $20M, CSDA Program task order $13.5M. Approximate run-rate ~$50-70M/yr federal contracts is consistent with U.S.-federal share of the $180.232M D&I segment (foreign government D&I — UK, Germany, Japan, NATO partners, Ukraine $35.9M — picks up the rest).
scores.interpretation: PASS. Federal contracts plus disclosed foreign government revenue (Ukraine $35.9M, planned SwAF low-9-figure multiyear) credibly fill the $180M D&I bucket. Growth trajectory consistent with addition of multi-year satellite services contracts.

scores.claim_text: $852.4M remaining performance obligations as of Jan 31, 2026; two customers 13% + 12% of revenue; one customer 33% of AR.
scores.M_check: Mode A: own 10-K confirms $852.4M RPO + concentration disclosure. Mode B: federal contract obligations ($165.5M across 89 awards) materially below RPO; unnamed Customer A (13%) and Customer B (12%) are not identifiable as a specific U.S. federal recipient from usaspending — top single award is NASA $20M (≈6.5% of FY26 revenue).
scores.M_value: RPO 10-K-confirmed (edgar_fts hit on '852.4 million remaining performance obligations'). Federal contracts $165.5M obligated is far below $852.4M RPO; gap is consistent with: (i) multi-year SwAF Pelican contract (low 9-figure, not on usaspending), (ii) Ukraine $35.9M revenue (foreign), (iii) NRO/NGA classified contracts (often not in public usaspending detail), (iv) NASA CSDA IDIQ ceiling not yet fully obligated. Customer concentration percentages (13% / 12%) align with the SwAF and likely NRO/NGA / DoD prime relationships — but Planet does NOT identify Customer A or B in the 10-K.
scores.interpretation: MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. RPO is internally consistent with the SwAF $9-figure deal plus federal IDIQ ceilings, but the absence of named major customers when two each represent >10% of revenue (and one is 33% of AR) is a disclosure-clarity gap. NRO/NGA classified payor would reasonably explain non-naming; the gap is mostly explainable but not fully transparent.

scores.claim_text: Multi-year low 9-figure SwAF Pelican satellite services contract announced Dec 2025.
scores.M_value: edgar_fts shows 3 hits within Planet's filings for 'Swedish Armed Forces' (8-K 2026-01-12 with ex99_1, 8-K 2026-03-19 ex99_1, and the 10-K). Broad search for 'Planet Labs' + 'Swedish Armed Forces' returns 22 hits including the Planet press-release 8-Ks. Counterparty (Swedish Armed Forces) is a foreign sovereign and not an SEC filer, so reverse-counterparty edgar_fts is not applicable. Press-release filings confirm contract existence at the announcement date.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Contract is contemporaneously disclosed via 8-K and reaffirmed in 10-K, and Planet's announcement is visible across multiple SEC filings. Counterparty is a foreign sovereign so no reciprocal SEC disclosure expected.

scores.claim_text: Seven acquisitions over a decade (BlackBridge, Terra Bella, Boundless Spatial, VanderSat, Salo Sciences, Sinergise, Bedrock).
scores.M_check: Mode A: each acquisition individually disclosed in 10-K notes (Sinergise, Salo, VanderSat in financials; Bedrock 8-K filed 2025-12-10). Mode B: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence on aggregate rollup with parent thesis.
scores.M_value: acq_coherence mean_coherence = 0.79 (COHERENT_ROLLUP), 0 low-coherence acquisitions, 0 revenue-synthetic flags. Individual scores: BlackBridge 0.95, Terra Bella 0.95, Boundless Spatial 0.65, VanderSat 0.65, Salo Sciences 0.65, Sinergise (high), Bedrock (high). Bedrock Research 8-K (2025-12-10) confirmed; APA $6.0M purchase price disclosed. edgar_fts 'Bedrock Research' returns 2 hits (8-K + 10-K).
scores.interpretation: PASS. Acquisition strategy is coherent (mean 0.79) and each deal is individually disclosed and integrates with the core EO/geospatial AI thesis. Bedrock $6M tuck-in is small but technology-aligned.

scores.claim_text: $460M 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 issued Sep 12, 2025; $445.8M net proceeds; $39.6M of capped calls.
scores.M_check: Mode A: SEC filings list (8-K on 2025-09-08, 09-10, 09-12) confirms the $460M convertible notes issuance. Mode B: insider_vs_calendar.query_insider_sales_near_budget_events(cik=0001836833, window_days=14, start_date=2024-01-01, end_date=2026-05-20).
scores.M_value: insider_vs_calendar signal = CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY. 53 Form 4 filings, 42 total sales totaling $68.2M; 17 sales ($28.77M) within ±14 days of budget/PB/fiscal events; 5 are discretionary (non-10b5-1) proximate sales by 7 unique insiders. Key proximate clusters: (a) FY25 fiscal-year-end Sep 30, 2025 — BASS CARL discretionary sale of 376,748 shares @ $15.67 = $5.9M on Oct 6 (6 days post-event); Marshall (CEO) 200K shares @ $15.50 = $3.1M (10b5-1) on Oct 13. (b) FY26 bipartisan budget signed Jan 20, 2026 — 13 sales totaling $17.26M including discretionary sales by Marshall (CEO), Johnson (CFO), Schingler (co-founder), Robinson, Gadde just days after the budget signing. (c) Bond/notes issuance Sep 12, 2025 — closely follows the Sep 30 fiscal year-end insider sale cluster.
scores.interpretation: SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY. The $460M raise itself is real and properly disclosed (PASS on Mode A), but Mode B reveals a CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY insider-selling pattern tied to fiscal-year-end and FY26 budget signing — including the CEO/CFO/co-founder discretionary sales within days of the bipartisan budget signing and within weeks of the convertible-note pricing. Per the prompt's heuristic, CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY is a SEVE-RED indicator. Marked SEVE (not RED) because most discretionary value is sub-$10M individually and a meaningful portion of total disposals are F-code tax withholdings on RSU vests rather than open-market opens. Still, the temporal coincidence of insider dispositions with the bipartisan budget signing and the convertible-note pricing is the highest-discrimination flag for this filing.

scores.claim_text: Patents covering novel features of our spacecraft underpin our IP portfolio.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee on 'Planet Labs' and 'Planet Labs PBC'
scores.M_value: Planet Labs assignee: 72 total applications, 28 granted patents pre-cutoff. Planet Labs PBC variant: 15 applications, 9 granted. Granted patents include 'Multi-Pathway Satellite Communication Systems and Methods' (US 12,284,024 granted 2025-04-22; US 12,199,737 granted 2025-01-14), 'Systems and Methods for Cloud Avoidance', 'Anisotropic Aperture Star Camera Systems', and a 'Vertically Integrated Backend' PCT — all topically aligned with on-orbit satellite operations, sensor processing, and constellation management.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Patent claim is corroborated — 28 granted patents under 'Planet Labs', all in claimed technology categories (spacecraft communications, sensor design, on-orbit data processing). Well above the heuristic n_granted >= 5 threshold.

scores.claim_text: HQ ~71,280 sq ft in San Francisco where satellite manufacturing, testing, R&D occur; additional manufacturing in Germany.
scores.M_value: EPA FRS in CA returned 1 facility named 'DEAR PLANET LABS, INC.' in Placentia, CA — that is NOT Planet Labs PBC (different entity); no Planet Labs PBC facility in FRS. OSHA established footprint: NO_OSHA_FOOTPRINT (0 matches). Note: per calibration heuristic 1, light electronics / satellite assembly typically NOT EPA-regulated and may not appear in OSHA establishments data depending on size — these are coverage gaps, not contradictions.
scores.interpretation: UNVERIFIABLE. EPA FRS and OSHA are not authoritative for SF-based satellite-assembly cleanrooms (no industrial emissions / no large headcount-reporting establishment). Heuristic 1 applies. Cannot flag absence.

scores.claim_text: ICFR was effective as of Jan 31, 2026; KPMG LLP issued integrated audit attestation.
scores.M_check: Mode A: in-filing assertion of effectiveness + KPMG attest. Mode B: claim_evolution(cik, 'material weakness', 2024-01-01 to 2026-05-20)
scores.M_value: claim_evolution evolution_status = MENTIONED_INCIDENTALLY: 6 subsequent mentions of 'material weakness' all classified UNRELATED (risk-factor boilerplate definitions, not actual identified weaknesses). No adverse_findings, no amendment_hits, no restatements. Historical edgar_fts 'material weakness' hits in Planet's CIK trace back to pre-merger dMY IV SPAC re-classifications (Nov 2021 10-Q/A) — those are pre-business-combination SPAC accounting issues, not current Planet ICFR.
scores.interpretation: PASS. No material weakness or adverse opinion in the relevant period. KPMG clean integrated-audit attestation confirmed in the 10-K. ICFR claim is clean.

scores.claim_text: Technology partnerships with NASA JPL, Carbon Mapper, and NASA Communications Services Project (with Telesat / SES).
scores.M_value: NASA NTRS signal = NASA_PUBLISHED. 202 total hits with 'Planet Labs', 3 filtered as primary including 'Geometric Assessment of PlanetScope Imagery' (Goddard, funding 80GSFC20C0044), and 'Assessment of Sensor Footprint Size and Comparison of Commercial Smallsat Images' (Goddard, same funding). Also 'high-spatiotemporal-resolution leaf area index ... using Planet Labs CubeSat'. Independently, NASA contracts to Planet Labs Federal include $20M ELECTRO OPTICAL DATA REQUIREMENT and $13.5M CSDA Program task order. No federal grants to PLF directly ($0M, expected — Planet is a vendor, not a grantee).
scores.interpretation: PASS. NASA partnership / Tanager-Carbon Mapper context is consistent with NASA Goddard scientific publications using PlanetScope and direct NASA contract awards. Civil-government NASA partner channel is real.
